## **Copper Monthly February 2012 No. 182** #### **Highlights** ##### **INSIDE THIS ISSUE** ###### **Chinese economic data** China's economy expanded by 9.2 percent in 2011 from a year earlier and 8.9 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). The quarterly growth was the slowest in 10 quarters. China set its full-year growth target at 8 percent in early 2011 after its economy grew 10.4 percent in 2010. China's fixed-asset investment rose 23.8 percent year-on-year to 30.1933 trillion yuan ($4.7736 trillion) in 2011. The growth rate was down 0.7 percentage points compared to that in the first 11 months, and remained flat from that of last year. On a monthly basis, fixed-asset investments fell 0.14 percent in December. China's consumer price index (CPI), a main gauge of inflation, rose 4.1 percent year-on-year in December, down 0.1 percentage point from November on falling non-food prices. The CPI was up 5.4 percent in 2011 from the previous year, well above the government's full-year inflation control target of 4 percent, the NBS said in a statement on its website. China's Producer Price Index (PPI), a major measure of inflation at the wholesale level, rose 1.7 percent in December year-on-year, further weakening from 2.7 a month earlier. On a month-on-month basis, China's December PPI fell 0.3 percent from November, the NBS said. #### **Copper Market Review 2011 and Outlook 2012** #### Copper prices review in 2011 The copper price bottomed at US$6,635/t on Oct. 3, the lowest level in 2011, and it fluctuated between US$7,000-9,000/t within the year. The Eurozone debt

crisis and the slowdown of China’s economy growth are the two key factors which can affect the metal market in 2011. The average copper price of cash month and 3-month dropped to US$7,488/t and US$7,510/t in Q4 2011, decreasing by 16.72% and 16.66% on a quarterly basis and declining by 13.29% and 12.85% on a yearly basis. But as the prices were higher in the first half compared with the corresponding period of the previous year, the annual average price was still above the level in 2010. The newly added smelting and refining capacity were much higher than that in 2010, which was another new expanding period for Chinese copper smelting/refining capacity. It is estimated that this kind of expanding situation will continue until 2013 and newly added smelting and refining capacity will exceed 600kt/y and 1Mt/y. Such kind of expansion for Chinese smelting and refining capacity has become key drivers for domestic refined copper growth and important factor that depressed TC/RCs. #### Copper- in-concentrate supply in a small shortage According to data from China Nonferrous metals Industry Association (CNIA), domestic copper-in-concentrate output during Jan to Dec 2011 was 1.27Mt, up by 9.6% y/y. Antaike estimates that total copper-in-concentrate output in 2011 will reach 1.25Mt, up by 9.6% y/y. Import volume in 2011 basically kept flat with that in 2010, at 1745kt. Copper-in-concentrate demand increased by 12.1% to 2933kt in 2011.

Domestic supply shortage was 63kt in 2011. 

Antaike estimates that copper-in-concentrate output in 2012 will keep rapid growth trend and import will return to growth. So it is possible for copper-in-concentrate supply to increase in 2012. But copper-in-concentrate demand will have a faster growth due to a new expanding round for Chinese copper smelting/refining capacity since 2011. Antaike estimates that copper-in-concentrate supply will still be in shortage in 2012 and the shortage will reach about 100kt.

#### Domestic secondary copper supply in surplus 

As the abolition of tax rebate for copper scraps, copper scraps prices have been losing its price advantage and began to be higher than refined copper prices after September 2011, which caused partial copper semis enterprises who use copper scraps as major raw materials in shutdown or in half shutdown. 

According to data from CNIA, Chinese secondary copper output was 1.73Mt in 2010, up by 25.2% y/y, accounting for 37.8% of total refined copper output, 4.2 percentage points higher than 2009. During Jan to Dec, domestic secondary copper output was 1.81Mt, a rise of 4.8% y/y, about 34.9% of the total refined copper output during this period. Decline of growth rate and proportion reflected the influence on domestic secondary copper production by above mentioned factors from one side. 

Copper scraps import was 4.69Mt (physical quantity) during Jan to Dec, up by 7.4% y/y. According to Antaike’s investigation, downstream enterprises had other channels to get copper scraps. On the whole, copper scraps market was in surplus, at about 60kt, and the surplus mainly appeared in H2 2011. 

#### Refined copper output increases rapidly, but consumption down 

According to data from State Statistics Bureau, domestic refined copper output during Jan to Dec was about 5.18Mt, up by 14.2% y/y. Data released by CNIA showed that refined copper output was 5.20M

t, up by 14.6% y/y. Calculated by above growth trend, refined copper output will reach 5.20Mt in 2011. 

Antaike has different idea from above institutions’. According to Antaike’s data, Chinese 12 refined copper enterprises whose refined copper output accounted for about 70% of the national total produced 3.87Mt refined copper during Jan to Dec 2011, up by 14.3% y/y. Antaike estimates that domestic refined copper output will be about 5.18Mt in 2011. 

Website: www.antaike.com

In respect of refined copper consumption, electric power industry and air conditioning and refrigeration industry made great contribution on the growth of copper consumption. Rural network reconstruction in 2011 raised investment in this industry, whose driving force for copper consumption was obvious. Benefited by such home appliances promotion policies, as Home Appliances to the Countryside, Traded in and Energy subsidies. Air conditioning and refrigeration industry had a rapid growth in 2011. As the implement of China’s real estate regulatory policy in 2011, total investment in real estate and new commenced area had a decline in growth, which is unfavorable for Chinese copper consumption. Growth rate slowdown of China’s autos, reduced investment in railway fundamental construction and less order forms in ship building industry gave great pressures on copper consumption in 2011 after continuous two year’s high growth in Chinese transportation industry. Electronics industry has a stable development in recent years. 

Data released by the NBS showed that copper semis output was 1.03Mt in Dec, down by 2.7% m/m. Antaike estimates that copper semis consumption will be suppressed at a relative degree because most of enterprises will make more attention to accounts recovery and claiming the debt at year end. 

According to statistic from China Electricity Council, total investment in electric power construction reached 739.3.7 bln yuan in 2011, almost the same level as last year. Of which investment in power source and power grid were 371.2 bln yuan and 368.2 bln yuan, down by 6.49% y-o-y or up by 6.77% y-o-y. This year investment in power grid kept a continuous rise while growth rate of investment in power source slowed down. Of investment in power source, investment in hydropower, thermal power, nuclear power and wind power were respectively 94.0 bln yuan, 105.4 bln yuan, 74.0 bln yuan and 82.9 bln yuan. 

Statistics from China Electricity Council still released that the newly added power generation capacity that has been put into operation in China was about 90.00 GW in 2011, including 12.25 GW of hydropower, 58.86 GW of thermal power and 19.28 GW of nuclear power, wind power and solar power. Antaike estimates that domestic refined copper consumption will reach 7.33Mt, up by 7.8% y/y, 4 percentage points lower than last year.

The situation was reversed in H2 2011. Refined copper export had a continuous growth and export declined apparently with the growth of restocking need. Refined copper export showed a high-low trend. Domestic refined copper export was 327kt during Jan to Dec, greatly up by 303.5% y/y. Refined copper export reached 147kt in H1 2011, up by 712.1% y/y, mainly due to lower domestic copper prices against international copper prices and destocking actions in domestic copper market. Economy trend is still an import factor which affects copper market. Debt problem in Euro Zone, China’s inflation and tight monetary policy, and various stimulus economic policies in USA, all these make great influence on the market. Indonesia Grasberg mine workers ended strike after Freeport bosses agreed to an increase in wages. Strikes happened in foreign mines increased worries about copper concentrate supply, which formed support for copper prices. Copper inventory on LME declined to about 370kt at the end of 2011, with a drop of about 108kt compared to 478kt on Jun 10, hitting the highest level in 2011. Cancelled warrants was in a high level, with the highest of over 60kt, at 44kt at the end of 2011, accounting for about 12% of inventory, a sign of continuous decline of inventory. Most of cancelled warrants came from warehouses in Korea and Singapore, indicating that these copper were shipped to China, caused by restocking need in China. Inventory on SHFE fell below 100kt after Oct, even below 60kt at the end of Nov. After that, inventory has a rise due to importing large number of refined copper. Inventory on SHFE maintained below 100kt. **Chart 4 Inventory and Closing Price of LME 3-month Copper** In the eyes of US dollar index in the whole year of 2011, it shook to rise, which is not a good piece of news for copper prices in Dollars. Website: www.antaike.com 9 Copper Monthly No. 182 **Chart 5 USD Index and LME 3 Copper Closing Price** #### Market Balance and Price Outlook ###### **Supply/demand** Antaike estimates that Chinese copper smelting and refining capacity will reach 4.72Mt and 8.23Mt in 2012, with newly added copper smelting and refining capacity of 650kt and

1.1Mt. 

Chinese copper concentrate production will keep a moderate growth in 2012. Chinese refined copper production is expected to keep a rapid growth as the rising supply of foreign raw material and domestic expanding copper capacity. It is estimated that refined copper production will reach 5.70Mt in 2012, with a growth rate of about 11%. 

According to the annual central economic work conference that closed on Dec 14, the main theme of next year's economic and social development will be making progress while maintaining stability. China's current economy remains good, but the domestic and international environment is extremely complicated. 

In 2012, the growth rate in most of copper using industries, such as air conditioning and refrigeration industry, housing industry, transportation industry and etc. will be lower than 2011. Domestic refined copper consumption in 2012 will reach 7.76Mt, up by below 6% against 2011. The growth rate will continue to drop. 

Refined copper import will have a continuous decline, but in a relative high level. It is difficult for Chinese refined copper in 2012 to recur large amount of export.

###### **Price Outlook in 2011** 

Macroeconomic picture is extremely unclear, which will maintain weak at least in H1 2012. It is difficult for global copper prices to have a unilateral rise in 2012. At the same time, global copper supply is still tight, which will form a support for copper price. 

It is expected that copper price will fluctuate at a high level in whole 2012, but there exist many uncertainties in H1 2012. 

In 2012 copper price on LME will keep a low-high trend, at an average price of US$ 8,000. Copper price on SHFE will be within a range of 45,000-70,000yuan/t, with the average price of 58,000yuan/t in 2012.
